action: opened the order: Invent one new widget that goes beyond everything in the catalog. One remarkable idea, or none.
Untapped capability: proposed Margin (margin-widget), Attic (attic-widget), Lightbox (lightbox-widget)
Person at the terminal: proposed Strays (strays-widget), Tripwire (tripwire-widget), Shorthand (shorthand-widget)
Delight: proposed Unsaid (unsaid-widget), Second Thoughts (doubt-widget), The Jar (jar-widget)
took the order at ideation
took the order at ideation

stamped reject on "Attic": The engine already puts MCP server tools behind ToolSearch by its own rule (ToolDescribeInput.isDeferred doc), so the dead weight it promises to remove is mostly gone already, and ToolInfo carries no schema so the sizes it would show are guesses.

stamped reject on "Strays": Attributing listeners by a port snapshot before and after every Bash call spawns a process per call, misses servers that bind after the call returns, and ends in a kill button on a guessed pid: cost and risk out of proportion to an occasional port-in-use message.

stamped reject on "Tripwire": A variation on what exists: vows-widget and stakes-widget already stop a matched command at the permission step with a reason, and notes-widget and capsule-widget already hold the person's reminder text.

stamped reject on "Shorthand": A variation on situation-widget and the built-in @ mention: it sends the same last-error and last-file facts with the prompt, only on a typed keyword, and needs a timer polling the prompt box to preview them.

stamped reject on "Unsaid": The longest deleted run is most often a mistaken paste, which can be a secret put back on screen, and the softened or sharpened tally is word-list guesswork, so the promised moment is rare and the common one is noise or exposure.

stamped reject on "Second Thoughts": It depends on a raw thinking stream that is often off or summarised, and matching 'actually' and 'wait' at sentence starts gives a count nobody can trust, so most sessions would show the empty state or noise.

stamped reject on "The Jar": A phrase counter with a picture is a variation on the reactive scenes and badges, and it rests on a short list of stock phrases that current models seldom say, so the jar would sit empty.

stamped reject on "Lightbox": Not chosen: it survives on novelty, but the Image element draws pixels only in kitty and Ghostty, so on most terminals, including Windows Terminal and tmux, and on the demo page, the card is a file name; Margin works wherever fullscreen does.
named the widget margin-widget ("Margin")

stamped pass: Margin is the only idea that gives the person a new way to act: annotate passages of Claude's reply by mouse selection and send them back as one quoted prompt, using ui.selection and Input which no widget has touched, at no token cost, on any terminal in fullscreen.
